109	## 4. Architecture decisions
110	
111	**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
112	`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
113	`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
114	card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).
115	
116	```
117	ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
118	  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
119	              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
120	  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
121	  'home':     —
122	  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
123	```
124	
125	`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
126	`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.
127	
128	The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`
129	(`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showRemove`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`,
130	`hoverSwapsImage`). That is what satisfies the extensibility AC: add a union member + a config row, touch no JSX.
131	
132	**The card is fluid, not 288px.** `gridSystem.ts` has `maxWidth: 'none'`. Figma's 288/179 are widths at the
133	reference artboards. The card fills its grid cell (`width: 100%`); the image holds ratio via `aspectRatio`.
134	Grid placement belongs to SFCC-80.
135	
136	**Mobile/desktop boundary = 768px** (`breakpoints.md`, 48em) — the only confirmed foundation breakpoint between
137	the 402 and 1440 artboards, and where the grid already goes 4→8 columns. `min-width` is inclusive, so the 768
138	artboard gets the desktop card. Every hover rule is additionally gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`
139	so a 768px touch tablet never gets hover-only content. See OQ-5.
140	
141	**Hover is CSS-only, keyed on `:hover, :focus-within`.** No React hover state — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer
142	move is a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` is not optional: WCAG 2.2 AA requires the revealed size selector and
143	arrows be keyboard-reachable. All reveal selectors live in one place, the organism's recipe root part, selecting
144	descendants by the shared `data-card-slot` constants. Molecules stay hover-agnostic.
145	
146	**One link per card (stretched-link).** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button —
147	nesting those in an `<a>` is invalid HTML and an a11y failure. The link wraps the product name only and carries
148	a `::after { position:absolute; inset:0 }` overlay; controls get `position:relative; z-index:1`. `href` arrives
149	pre-prefixed from the page. Uses `import {Link as RouteLink} from 'react-router-dom'` per `zimmColourSwatch` —
150	there is no `overrides/app/components/link/` override, contrary to a claim in `overrideStyling.md`.
151	
152	**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` (`bag`, `close`, `chevron-left`,
153	`chevron-right` all exist in `ICON_MAP`). No new icons.
154	
155	**VIC pricing is not a card concern** — precedence is the page mapper's job. Deferred to SFCC-778 (OQ-6).

159	## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
160	
161	> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*
162	
163	The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:
164	
165	**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
166	`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:
167	
168	- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
169	- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.
170	
171	Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
172	and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
173	card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
174	a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
175	indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.
176	
177	**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**
178	
179	1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
180	   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
181	   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
182	   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
183	   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.
184	2. **Step 4 — mobile image paging has no mechanism and no AC.** If the indicator shows position on touch, some
185	   touch gesture must change the image. No AC covers this; the ACs only describe desktop hover. See OQ-11.
186	
187	---
188	
189	## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
190	
191	> *"scroll-snap it is"*
192	
193	Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
194	no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.
195	
196	**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**
197	
198	The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
199	`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
200	over it:
201	
202	| | Mechanism | Affordance |
203	|---|---|---|
204	| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
205	| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |
206	
207	One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
208	arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
209	keyboard scrollability for free.
210	
211	**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
212	PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
213	`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
214	event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.
215	
216	**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
217	(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
218	`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.
219	
220	**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
221	universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
222	invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile
223	gesture is undocumented in the design**, so it lands in the spec rather than being discovered in QA.
224	
225	**Added Step 4 pass criteria:**
226	- The slide container carries `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`; every slide carries `scrollSnapAlign`.
227	- Arrows are rendered only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; the indicator only outside it; assert the
228	  two never coexist in the same DOM.
229	- Arrow activation moves the scroll position (assert `scrollBy`/`scrollTo` is called — jsdom does not lay out,
230	  so assert the call, not the resulting offset).
231	- The indicator's active index tracks the observed slide, and clamps at both ends.
232	- A single-image product renders no indicator, no arrows, and no horizontal overflow.
233	- No gesture library is added — `package.json` is untouched (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7).
234	
235	---
236	
237	## 4c. Badge — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02), and it corrects the decomposition
238	
239	Nine nodes supplied; all resolve off one parent, `40001471:20702` "Badge" (a documentation board).
240	`40001471:20682` is its cover slide, not a component.
241	
242	**There are TWO badge components, not one:**
243	
244	| Component set | Node | Variants | Size |
245	|---|---|---|---|
246	| **`Badge`** | `40001471:20752` | `State=Primary` (`…20751`) · `State=Hover` (`…20750`) | 33×15 |
247	| **`Stock Status Badge`** | `40001796:7041` | `State=Available` (`…7040`) · `State=Unavailable` (`…7039`) · `State=Low stock` (`…7038`) | 66–79×20 |
248	
249	`Stock Status Badge` appears in **no acceptance criterion**. It maps to `.docs/prd/plp.md` §3
250	("**OUT OF STOCK** shown on tile when all sizes are at or below buffer threshold" and the low-stock
251	indicator) — so the PRD requirement that had no design **does** have one. Its `Low stock` state
252	corresponds to nothing in any AC, and `plp.md` §3 places low-stock *at size level*, not on the tile.
253	
254	### Decomposition correction — three slots move from Content to Media
255	
256	Reading `Image Group / Size=Large` (`40002742:46322`, 288×432) and `Size=Small` (`40002742:46321`,
257	179×268) shows the overlays live on the **image**, not in the text block:
258	
259	| Slot | Frame | Structure | Desktop | Mobile |
260	|---|---|---|---|---|
261	| **`Tag`** (the badge) | 78×48 @ top-left | `touchContainer` 30×24 @ (24,12) → `Label` text 30×8 | ✅ | ✅ |
262	| **`Close`** (remove 'x') | 48×48 @ top-right | `touchContainer` 24×24 → `Icon` 16×16 | ✅ | ✅ |
263	| **`Carousel`** (arrows) | 288×24 @ y=204 (vertically centred) | two `touchContainer` 24×24 @ x=12 and x=252 | ✅ | **absent** |
264	| **`Slide-indicator`** | 179×1, flush to the image's bottom edge (y=267 of 268) | instance | **absent** | ✅ |
265	
266	**Consequences:**
267	
268	1. **The badge slot moves from Step 5 to Step 4.** It is `Tag`, overlaid top-left on the image — not a part
269	   of `Card-content`. Remove the `badge` part from `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`; add a `tag` part to
270	   `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`.
271	2. **The remove ('x') CTA moves from Step 5 to Step 4.** It is `Close`, top-right on the image. The plan had
272	   it in `ZimmProductCardContent` — wrong molecule. Remove `onRemove` handling from Content; it belongs in
273	   Media. The union still carries `onRemove` on the wishlist member; the organism passes it to Media.
274	3. **This makes the split cleaner, not messier:** everything overlaid on the image is Media, everything below
275	   it is Content.

Compiles and passes — CLEAN ``` npx tsc --noEmit → zero output, exit clean npm run test -- --run → Test Files 54 passed (54) / Tests 871 passed (871) node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs → 1 unacknowledged violation total, in overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:20 ('59.125em') — pre-existing, not touched by this diff. One in-scope acknowledged exception: `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts:40` (`width: '65px'`) carries a correct `audit-allow:` comment per convention — clean. **Angle clean. No findings here.** --- ## 2. 🔴 The "recently viewed carousel" badge/hover-swap suppression has no code path — CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF (but high blast-radius) This was the specific tension the task asked me to resolve. I resolved it: **the gap is real.** - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx:213-216` — `ZimmProductCardVariation` has exactly three members: `'plp' | 'home' | 'wishlist'`. - `index.tsx:276-316` — `VARIATION_CONFIG` has exactly three keys (`home`, `plp`, `wishlist`). `plp.showBadge = true`, `plp.showHoverImageSwap = true`. - `index.tsx:125-126` mirrors plan.md's own text (plan.md:125-127): *"'recently-viewed' is not a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass `variation: 'plp'`."* But this AC-equivalence statement is about **SFCC-236's own "Recently Viewed Full History" variation** (the AC text findings.md's gate update quotes: *"same behavior as PLP card"*) — i.e. SFCC-84's page-level grid. It is a **different consumer** from findings.md gate item #17: Dani Rivett's comment (Jira comment 13880, 14 Aug) that *"we do not want the badge displayed on the Homepage **or** on the Recently Viewed product carousel"* and *"we don't want the hover action (model photo) on the homepage **or** the recently viewed carousel"* — i.e. SFCC-83's rail. The shipped code (commit `5802802`, index.tsx:86-120 docblock) demonstrably used this exact Dani comment as its authority for suppressing badge/hover-swap on `home` — it quotes it twice ("Per Dani Rivett's scope note", "Dani's comment also says 'we don't want the hover action... on the homepage'") — but **only ever implements the Home half of a two-part sentence.** I grepped every touched file (component, test, story, docblock) for `carousel` (in the rail sense), `SFCC-83`, and `Dani` in combination — the only "carousel" hits anywhere in the shipped code are the **Media molecule's own arrow-button wrapper**, an unrelated same-word collision (`zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` `data-card-slot="carousel"`, `zimmProductCard.css.ts:11,208,215`). Nowhere does the code, a test, a story, or an OQ entry acknowledge that half of Dani's comment remains unaddressed. Consequence: **a future SFCC-83 consumer has no way to get the suppression Dani asked for.** Per plan's own precedent (`variation: 'plp'` for the AC-equivalent Full History case), the natural thing for whoever builds SFCC-83 next to do is reach for `variation: 'plp'` again — and inherit `showBadge: true` / `showHoverImageSwap: true`, the opposite of the written instruction. `home` isn't a substitute either — it suppresses the bag button and uses `hoverRevealsPrice` instead of `hoverHidesPrice`, which is wrong for a PLP-shaped rail tile. This matters more than a normal "known gap" because **plan.md and findings.md live outside the repository** (`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/`, not `.docs/`), so gate finding #17's own suggested resolutions ("Add the rail variation to SFCC-236's ACs, or state that SFCC-83 owns its own tile") are invisible to anyone reviewing the actual PR or codebase. Nothing in the shipped code's docblocks, OQ references, or "Known gaps" carries this forward. **🔴 must-fix (as a documentation/traceability gap, not a wrong AC for SFCC-236 itself, since SFCC-83 is out of scope) — CONFIRMED — ONE-OFF.** Minimal fix: one sentence in `index.tsx`'s module docblock stating explicitly that the carousel-tile half of Dani's comment is deliberately unaddressed and belongs to SFCC-83, so it isn't lost the way it currently is. --- ## 3. 🔴 `zimmProductCardShared.ts` was never created — the promised single source of truth doesn't exist — CONFIRMED, UNIFORM Task instructions asked me to check whether `data-card-slot` constants and `CARD_BP` are "actually imported everywhere they're needed, or re-typed anywhere" in `zimmProductCardShared.ts`. **That file does not exist anywhere in the repository** — confirmed via `find`/`grep -rl` returning nothing. This directly contradicts the plan: - plan.md:96, 103-105: *"`zimmProductCardShared.ts` holds DOM-contract constants (`data-card-slot` names) + `CARD_BP`... Keeps the Tier 2 surface at exactly one file."* - plan.md:490-491 (Step 6): *"Creates `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, the union, `VARIATION_CONFIG`... and `zimmProductCard.css.ts`..."* - Plan explicitly cites this repo's own established precedent for exactly this situation: `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts` (which I read — a real, if tiny, one-constant file) and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "Cross-file shared values" section, which states in terms that match this exact defect shape: *"Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files; that's exactly the drift risk... already warns about."* Consequence, verified directly — **two categories of value are duplicated with no shared source, enforced only by a "don't forget" comment:** **(a) `data-card-slot` slot-name strings** (10 distinct literals: `media`, `badge`, `close`, `carousel`, `indicator`, `content`, `bag`, `price`, `sizeChips`, `notifyMe`). Each is: - Stamped as a raw JSX string in the producing molecule — `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:219,267,276,285,306`; `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:207,214,242,252,262`. - Independently re-typed as a raw string inside CSS selector strings in the consuming organism recipe — `zimmProductCard.css.ts:187,208,215,218,234,241,249,261,263,275,280,285,300-302,310,333,343` (17+ occurrences). - Re-typed again in `querySelector('[data-card-slot="..."]')` calls across three `.test.tsx` files. - The only synchronization mechanism is a comment: `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:8` and `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:15` both literally say *"Do not rename these values without updating that recipe too"* — i.e., the codebase has explicitly named the exact risk that a shared constants module exists to eliminate, and shipped the comment instead of the module. **(b) `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)'`** — independently defined as an unexported module-private `const` in **both** `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts:13` and `zimmProductCard.css.ts:11`.
